applied.quote: Sales tax rules sit outside card fees, and our [sales tax vs. use tax](/compare/sales-tax-vs-use-tax/) comparison covers them.
applied.replacement: Our [sales tax vs. use tax](/compare/sales-tax-vs-use-tax/) comparison covers sales tax rules.
applied.why: SOURCE says nothing about sales tax relative to card fees.

applied.quote: Helcim does not publish interchange as a number, so we left Helcim out of the modeled totals.
applied.replacement: Helcim does not publish interchange as a number, and Helcim is not part of the modeled totals.
applied.why: SOURCE gives a different exclusion reason (quote-based pricing).

applied.quote: Stripe's 2.9% + 30¢ produces a total that can be computed before a sale clears, so a seller who wants a fixed per-sale cost gets it from Stripe.
applied.replacement: Stripe's flat 2.9% + 30¢ gives a per-sale cost that can be computed from the ticket, so a seller who wants a fixed per-sale cost gets it from Stripe.
applied.why: SOURCE says nothing about sale clearing timing.

applied.quote: At high volume, price stops being a reason to pick either Authorize.net or Stripe.
applied.why: Evaluative conclusion not stated in SOURCE.

applied.quote: Clover therefore sits outside the modeled totals.
applied.replacement: Clover sits outside the modeled totals.
applied.why: SOURCE gives a different exclusion reason (quote-based pricing).

applied.quote: Add that monthly figure to Clover's per-sale fees before comparing a month's total with Stripe's no-monthly-fee pricing.
applied.replacement: Add any device plan cost to Clover's per-sale fees before comparing a month's total with Stripe's no-monthly-fee pricing.
applied.why: SOURCE does not say device plans are billed monthly.

applied.quote: Stripe lists developers and online sellers as its fit.
applied.replacement: Stripe's best fit is developers and online sellers.
applied.why: SOURCE records a best-fit field, not that Stripe itself lists it.

applied.quote: If international buyers are a real share, Stripe's extra 1.5% shows up on the first statement, and that's the month to price Paddle against it.
applied.replacement: If international buyers are a real share, Stripe's extra 1.5% raises your per-sale cost, so that's when to price Paddle against it.
applied.why: SOURCE says nothing about statements or their timing.

applied.quote: Stripe had the lowest monthly total in all three, because each rival either matches its rate and adds a monthly fee or charges a higher rate per sale.
applied.replacement: Stripe had the lowest monthly total in all three.
applied.why: Square Plus, Authorize.net, Shopify match the rate; Square Free, Paddle, Managed Payments charge more.

applied.quote: At The Modern Wallet, we modeled each provider's published fees across three online shop sizes at a $50 average ticket.
applied.replacement: At The Modern Wallet, we modeled published fees across three online shop sizes at a $50 average ticket.
applied.why: Helcim and Clover were excluded from the model, so not each provider.

applied.quote: Helcim's margin falls as volume grows: $0.425 per $50 sale at $60,000 a month and $0.375 at $200,000.
applied.replacement: In the modeled counterexample, Helcim's margin is $0.425 per $50 sale at $60,000 a month and $0.375 at $200,000.
applied.why: These figures come from the evidence counterexample, not from a published Helcim tier.

applied.quote: Clover fits retail sellers with small keyed-in tickets or sales that qualify for the 2.3% rate.
applied.why: SOURCE gives no fit for Clover; qualifying sales are unknown.

applied.quote: If international buyers are a real share, Stripe's extra 1.5% raises your per-sale cost, so that's when to price Paddle against it.
applied.why: SOURCE gives no Paddle international pricing to support this recommendation.
